## What the papers show (headline)

Scores sit at **14/20 on both papers** and the pattern is consistent:

1. **Time management is the main leak.** On both 09/16 papers he rushed or blanked the last stretch
   (Q16–20: "ran out of time", one question skipped, several "educated guess"). Roughly 4–6 marks per paper
   are lost to the clock, not to ability. → a **timing drill** (last 5 questions in 15 min) matters more than
   new content.
2. **Paper 2 (reasoning) — he second-guesses.** Many "C or D?", "B?", "E??" — he reaches the right region but
   cannot *confirm*. → drill **verification methods** (test a value, check a boundary), not more theory.
3. **Topic gaps** — the **09/04 audit** sharpened these. Almost every wrong/flagged question sits in one of
   three areas: **coordinate geometry (circles & the plane)**, **differentiation / stationary points**, and
   **range / max–min of rational & trig functions**. Below those: logs, ceiling integrals, and trig in
   unfamiliar form. See the **[09/04 error audit](set_2026-09-04.qmd)** for the question-by-question map.

His weak list overlaps ~90 % with the existing clinics, so lessons should **reuse** them rather than rebuild.

## What each flagged question actually was — open only after attempting the clinic

*Kept closed on purpose: several of these state the answer.*

| # | Clinic | The questions, and what they turned on |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | Triangles | **P2 Q11** — "educated guess": two triangles fit, so the answer is a range of $x$, not a value. |
| **1** | Unfamiliar graphs | **P1 H′** — $\log_2$ of a trig expression; **P2** — symmetry and transformations of an unfamiliar curve. |
| **2** | Coordinate geometry | **09/04 P1 B** — 100 concentric circles; he answered $\sqrt{10}$, the answer is $10$ (now Q13 in the clinic). **J** — two circles tangent to one line. **J′** — a quadrilateral via distances. **P2 Q10** — the region $\lvert y-x^{2}\rvert<2$ with $x+y<4$. **09/16 P1 Q7** — a locus, which is beyond the TMUA spec. |
| **3** | Necessary & sufficient | **Q1** — the exact condition is $p<1$, and the option $\lvert p\rvert<1$ sits strictly inside it, so it is *sufficient but not necessary*. **Q11**, **Q7** ("necessarily true"), **09/16 Q5** and **Q13**. |
| **4** | Converse & contrapositive | **Q16** — the three-lever safe. "Which **must** be true" wants the contrapositive; the converse is the trap option. |
| **5** | Spot the error | **Q5** — the proof dies at $n=1$, where $n^{2}+2=3$ is prime. **Q17** — first bad line is 7. **Q3** — $\sqrt{x-3}<x-2$; in fact the attempt is valid. **09/16 Q4**. |
| **6** | Scrambled proofs | Nothing flagged. The format is **rare** — one TMUA question in eight years, **2016 P2 Q7**, now worked as [S6 Q11](../../toolkit/s06_scrambled_proofs.qmd). |
:::

## Two topic sessions worth memorising

Built from an eight-year audit of Paper 2 (2016–2023). **Divisors/primes** and **plane shapes asked as
logical conditions** appear in every sitting and are never set as calculations — so they reward straight
memorisation, which suits a four-week run-in:

- **[T1 · Divisors & primes](../../toolkit/t01_divisors_primes.qmd)** — ten facts, eight quick checks.
  Covers his 09/04 **Q5** and **Q17** from the other side.
- **[T2 · Shapes as logical conditions](../../toolkit/t02_shapes_as_logic.qmd)** — the quadrilateral
  lattice and the diagonal table. Directly relevant to his flagged **quadrilateral equal-sides** question.
:::

*(Bigger than any single clinic: his **pace** — last 5 questions in 15 min — and, on Paper 2, **confirming**
an answer instead of guessing. Drill those alongside every session.)*
